extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents, and patent examiners handling foreign-language (non-Korean) patent applications before KIPO
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for submission, correction, and examination of Korean translations of foreign-language patent applications (including PCT filings) before the Korean Intellectual Property Office, focusing on new-matter evaluation and effects of translations/corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for Korean translations of divisional/converted applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If a divisional application or a converted application is filed in a foreign language, the Korean translations shall be submitted within 30 days from the date of a divisional or a converted application being filed, even though the period of 1 year and 2 months have already been lapsed from the filing date of the parent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations must be submitted within 30 days of filing the divisional/converted application (special rule regardless of earlier parent-application deadlines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and nature of Korean translations to be submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: The Korean translations shall be submitted accompanied by document submission form [Article 21(3) of the Exceptional Provisions to the Patent Act, Form No. 13], and the Korean translations of a foreign language specification (a “word-for-word translation” into Korean in accordance with the context of the foreign language specification) shall be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit Form No.13 and provide a word-for-word Korean translation consistent with the original context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to submit Korean translation of specification = withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Korean translations of foreign language specification are not submitted, the patent application concerned shall be deemed to have been withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omission of the required Korean translation of the specification results in the application being treated as withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to submit Korean translation of drawings (text captions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Korean translations of drawing(s) (the text matter only) are not submitted, the patent application concerned shall not be deemed to have been withdrawn as is different from the case of a specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-submission of drawing captions does not withdraw the application, but amendment may be instructed on grounds of violation of the written description requirement of drawing(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of submitting Korean translations — translations deemed to amend specification
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Korean translations are submitted, a foreign language specification originally attached to the application thereof shall be deemed to have been amended according to the Korean translations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Korean translations are 'awarded effects of amending the specification' to reduce applicants' burdens; examiners and the public will rely on the Korean text to define scope of rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-2015 rule on legal status of Korean translation vs foreign-language specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to a patent application filed in a language other than Korean under the amended Patent Act (Enforced on January 1, 2015), the Korean translations submitted shall not be regarded as a specification, but a foreign language specification shall be deemed to be amended with the submission of the filed Korean translations, from the applicant’s point of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although translations are not formally 'the specification', submission causes the foreign-language spec to be treated as amended according to the Korean translation for applicant-side effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary basis for new-matter evaluation: Korean translation
rubrics_metrics.description: To evaluate whether new matter is introduced in a specification and drawing(s) of the foreign language patent application ... shall basically be based on the scope of the disclosure of the Korean translations unless exceptional circumstances have occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners generally evaluate new-matter questions against the Korean translation rather than the original foreign-language text, except in special/doubtful cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: When mistranslations are corrected — evaluation basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the mistranslation is corrected, introduction of new matter shall be examined based on the Korean translations, but depending on appropriateness of correction of mistranslations, it shall be evaluated based on the foreign language specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If correction is made, examiner uses the corrected Korean translation as the evaluation baseline; appropriateness of the correction may require reference to the original foreign-language specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination where no correction of mistranslation is made
rubrics_metrics.description: Where no correction of mistranslation is made, it shall be sufficient for the examiner to examine whether a specification and drawing(s) under examination are within the scope of the Korean translations, without examining whether the specification or drawing(s) amended according to the Korean translations is within the scope of the disclosure of the foreign language patent application, unless there are considerable events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no correction filed, examiner need not compare to original foreign text in ordinary cases; focus is on conformity to the submitted Korean translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination where correction of mistranslation is made
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a correction of mistranslations is made, the examiner shall closely examine whether an amendment to the specification under examination is made within the scope of the disclosure of the foreign language specification or corrected Korean translations. In other words, introduction of new matter in a specification and drawing(s) subject to examination shall be closely evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When corrections are submitted, the examiner must scrutinize whether amendments exceed either the corrected translation or the original foreign-language disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments must be within original disclosure (Article 47(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment to the specification or drawings ... shall be made within the scope of the disclosure of the specification or drawings as originally filed. An amendment to a foreign language patent application shall be also made within the scope of the disclosures of the final Korean translation ... as originally filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment is limited to what was originally disclosed in the filing (including final Korean translation where applicable); exceeding that scope is grounds for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for rejection when amendment exceeds scope
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner shall make a decision to reject a patent application if ... an amendment to the patent application exceeds the scope described in Article 47 (2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments going beyond the allowed scope trigger rejection under Article 62; similar ground exists for invalidation trials (Article 133).

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of new matter relative to Korean translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment to a specification or drawing(s) under examination does not comply with Article 47(2) ... it shall be considered to introduce new matter beyond the scope of the disclosure of the Korean translations ... (i) Where a correction of mistranslations is not made: new matters beyond the scope of the Korean translations ... (ii) Where a correction of mistranslations is made: new matters which are disclosed in the final Korean translation, of which mistranslation has been corrected, are introduced ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish whether mistranslation correction was made when assessing whether introduced matter goes beyond the Korean translation(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment within foreign-language disclosure but beyond Korean translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment is made within the scope of disclosure of a foreign language specification but beyond the scope of the Korean translations, it shall constitute grounds for rejection but not grounds for invalidation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If amendment matches original foreign-language disclosure but exceeds the submitted Korean translation, rejection may be issued but it does not automatically create invalidation grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit/inherent disclosure counts as disclosure of translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for evaluating new matter ... shall be the same with the one for assessing a new matter for the regular amendment. Therefore, besides the explicit disclosure of the Korean translations, implicit or inherent disclosure of the Korean translations shall be treated as the 'disclosure of the Korean translation'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both explicit and implicit (inherent) disclosures in the translation are considered when assessing new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant responses to notice of new-matter beyond Korean translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where rejection on the ground of the introduction of new matter beyond the disclosure of the Korean translations is issued, a patent applicant shall make a response ... (i) submit a written argument that new matter is not introduced; (ii) delete the new matter by amending specification/drawings; (iii) submit correction of a mistranslation attaching documentary material and argue that new matter will be resolved by correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may argue, amend to remove offending content, or correct mistranslation with supporting documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: New-matter beyond foreign-language specification prohibited (grounds for rejection & invalidation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction of new matter in the Korean translations beyond the disclosure of the foreign language specification submitted on the filing date ... is not permitted ... Such a 'new matter beyond the disclosure of the foreign language specification' constitutes grounds for rejection (Article 62(5) ) and grounds for invalidation (Article 133(1)vi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New matter relative to the original foreign-language filing is treated like new matter in regular applications — may lead to rejection and post-grant invalidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for evaluating new matter relative to foreign-language specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria ... is the same with the one applied in a regular patent application. In other words, it shall be evaluated whether the matters described in the specification under examination are explicitly disclosed in the foreign language specification or implicitly or inherently disclosed in the foreign language specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply same explicit/implicit disclosure tests as for regular amendments when comparing to the foreign-language original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence-order changes in translation do not necessarily create new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the Korean translations are filed by changing the order of the sentences in the foreign language specification and thus the specification is deemed to be amended as in the Korean translations, where new matter, which is not included in the foreign language specification, is not introduced in the specification, it shall not constitute new matter in the original text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reordering or stylistic differences in translation are acceptable provided no substantive new matter is introduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to compare foreign-language specification with Korean translation/spec-for-exam
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner shall have to evaluate proscription against introduction of new matter as taking into account the foreign language specification mainly in the following cases: (1) where information indicates the spec submitted for examination includes new matter beyond the foreign language spec and there is reasonable doubt; (2) where international preliminary examination report or family-filed arguments disclose new matter; (3) where third parties provide reasonable information that new matter is introduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reasonable doubt or external information exists, examiner compares original foreign-language filing and the translation/impugned specification; otherwise rely mainly on translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for correcting a mistranslation — documents required
rubrics_metrics.description: A person ... intending to correct errors of the Korean translation under Article 42(3)vi, shall submit a statement of correction of a mistranslation attaching relevant documents ... and pay relevant fees ... (required: statement of correction; power of attorney as patent agent appointed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction must follow prescribed administrative procedure: statement, documentary evidence, (if applicable) power of attorney, and fee payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive documentary requirements for correction of mistranslation
rubrics_metrics.description: The documentary materials shall clearly describe (i) the matters described in the foreign language specification originally attached to the patent application are comparable to the amendment, (ii) inappropriateness of the Korean translation before amendment, (iii) appropriateness of the Korean translation after amendment (reasons for correction), so that a skilled person shall confirm correction is not beyond the matters described in the original foreign language patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentary materials must objectively justify the correction and show comparability to the original foreign-language disclosure so a skilled person can confirm no new matter is introduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: When correction of mistranslation is unnecessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Even though the Korean translation is wrongly translated, if matters thereof can be obviously understood from the Korean translation, the mistranslation shall not have to be corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If meaning is clear despite a mistranslation, correction may be unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of correction: corrected translation used for new-matter tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Korean translation is corrected as it has mistranslation, introduction of new matter beyond the disclosure of the Korean translation shall be examined based on the corrected Korean documents (final version of the Korean translation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrected (final) Korean translation becomes the baseline for assessing whether subsequent amendments introduce new matter (subject to appropriateness checks against the original foreign text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrected Korean translation during amendment period does not itself amend the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction of Korean translations made during the period for amending a specification or drawings is not given an amendment effect ... the corrected Korean translation due to mistranslation under Article 42(3)vi shall not have the same effect with the amendment to the specification or drawing(s). Therefore, where the Korean translation has mistranslation, amendment to a specification for examination shall be made, irrespective of the correction of the Korean translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants still must amend the specification itself where needed; correcting the Korean translation during amendment period does not automatically change the specification for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination procedure where correction is reasonable — outcomes depend on whether spec amended
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the corrected Korean translation sufficiently conforms to a foreign language specification as correction is confirmed reasonable, examination differs depending on whether a specification for examination is amended or not: (i) if spec for examination is not amended: a notification of grounds for rejection shall be issued in violation of introduction of new matter beyond the foreign language specification and the Korean translation; (ii) if spec for examination is amended within scope of matters described in the corrected Korean translation: regular examination continues; if amendment is beyond scope of corrected translation: grounds for rejection shall be closely reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If correction is reasonable and applicant amends the spec within the corrected translation, normal examination proceeds; otherwise rejections are considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination procedure where correction is unreasonable — outcomes differ
rubrics_metrics.description: Where mistranslation is improperly corrected so that corrected Korean translation does not conform to the foreign language specification, examination differs depending on whether a specification is amended or not: (i) if spec for examination is not amended and identical with un-corrected translation: issue notice of grounds for rejection that spec does not fall within scope of Korean translation or original foreign application; (ii) if spec is amended based on correction of mistranslation: rejection on ground of introduction of new matter beyond the original foreign language patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unreasonable corrections can lead to rejection based on mismatch with either the Korean translation or the original foreign-language disclosure; specifics depend on whether the exam spec was amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proscribed categories of new-matter after corrections/amendments (beyond foreign spec / beyond Korean translation / beyond both)
rubrics_metrics.description: 3.4.2.1 Proscription beyond the foreign language specification: where correction and amendment still leave spec beyond scope of foreign-language spec, rejection on ground of introduction of new matter beyond foreign-language specification. 3.4.2.2 Proscription beyond the Korean translation: where no errors in Korean translation but unnecessary correction makes translation different from foreign spec and spec remains un-amended, rejection issued for introduction beyond Korean translation. 3.4.2.3 Proscription beyond both: where spec amended and translations corrected but final corrected translation still differs from foreign-language spec and spec for examination is amended beyond corrected translations and foreign spec, rejection issued on ground of introduction beyond both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify which baseline (foreign spec, Korean translation, or both) the amendment exceeds; rejection will be issued accordingly and applicant must correct the correction and/or amend the specification back into conformity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations re: sufficiency of documentary materials for correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Where documentary materials accompanied by a statement of correction do not explain reasons for correction or reasons are not sufficiently described so that appropriateness of correction is hard to evaluate, amendment shall be ordered on the ground of insufficient reasons for correction, and appropriateness shall be evaluated after translation errors are resolved through amendment. If amendment cannot relieve insufficient reasons for correction, correction of mistranslations itself shall be invalidated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentary support must be adequate; otherwise the Office may order amendments, and may ultimately invalidate the correction if insufficiently justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness/inappropriateness of correction per se not automatic ground for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a mistranslation is corrected, appropriateness and inappropriateness thereof shall not constitute reasons for rejection or reasons for amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merely arguing that a correction is appropriate/ inappropriate does not alone justify rejection; substantive assessment and necessary procedural remedies apply.
